item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Sharpen a Blurry Dog Photo

turns.text: This phone pic of my dog came out blurry. Can you make it clearer and bigger, 640 pixels on the long side? Keep it looking natural.

item.tests: Enhances a blurry supplied photo rather than replacing its subject or merely enlarging the blur.

answer_sheet.Enhancement style: Natural-looking blur reduction and sharpening, not a stylised remake.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: 640 pixels on the long side; preserve the original proportions and framing.
answer_sheet.Subject and background: Keep the same dog, pose, expression, and background.

must_haves: The same golden retriever from blurry-dog.jpg remains recognisable in the same pose.
The dog's visible contours and facial features are clearer than in the blurry source.
Fur and edges look natural, without pronounced sharpening halos or invented decorative detail.
The background and full original framing are preserved.
The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.

turns.text: can you fix this pic of my dog
turns.agent:
I couldn't fix the photo. Your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was made and nothing was charged.

I tried three things, and each was refused for lack of credits:
1. **AI upscale, "balanced" mode:** the best option for blurry photos, because it rebuilds detail.
2. **AI upscale, "preserve" mode:** costs half as much as balanced.
3. **AI image edit (flux-2-klein, 640px):** the cheapest option, from about 5 credits per image. It redraws the photo in focus, aiming for the same dog, pose and park background.

**What you can do:**
- **Add credits** with a credit pack or a plan upgrade in your Magic Hour account. Then tell me and I'll run the upscale again; it's the best fit for this photo. The 2x upscale costs 25–200 credits depending on mode, and you may need a paid plan for the higher-quality modes.
- **Wait for your free credits to refill,** if your free plan refills them, and ask me again then.

The photo is very blurry, so any AI fix will have to invent some detail, like the fur and eyes. The result should look like your dog, but some small details may not match exactly.
